short: In six years he built the NHS, the welfare state and an independent India.
full:
Clement Attlee's Labour government, elected by a landslide in July 1945 while Churchill was still at Potsdam, carried out the most extensive peacetime programme of any British administration. The National Health Service opened on 5 July 1948, free at the point of use. The National Insurance and National Assistance Acts built a contributory safety net, and coal, rail, steel, gas, electricity and the Bank of England were taken into public ownership.

The same government granted independence to India and Pakistan in August 1947, withdrew from Palestine, helped found NATO in 1949, ran the Berlin airlift and secretly began a British atomic bomb. It did all this while effectively bankrupt, dependent on an American loan and imposing rationing tighter than wartime; bread was rationed in 1946, which it never had been during the war. Rearmament for Korea split the cabinet, and Labour lost office in October 1951 despite winning more votes than the Conservatives.
